recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reopening FHIR-14714 would be redundant unless BR&R identifies a new, concrete current ambiguity in RegulatedAuthorization beyond the already-applied R5/R6 wording decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-14714 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request raised against STU3 MedicinalProductAuthorization. It said the 2018Jan ballot resource had insufficient Description of Resource and Scope and Usage documentation and asked that it be improved before formal ballot; BR&R later agreed that substantial improvements were planned for R5.
initial_application: No commit mentioning FHIR-14714 was found in the FHIR source history. The old MedicinalProductAuthorization source initially had only a one-sentence scope statement and was then replaced during R5/R4B medication-definition work by RegulatedAuthorization; subsequent source history added broader RegulatedAuthorization content and removed the old MedicinalProductAuthorization source.
additional_context: The current build actively includes RegulatedAuthorization in source/fhir.ini, maps MedicinalProductAuthorization to RegulatedAuthorization for history/name tracking, and the history page documents the R4B rename. Later BR&R work, especially FHIR-29672, refined the same RegulatedAuthorization wording for R5; related wording proposals FHIR-28199 and FHIR-28576 were retracted/no-change rather than requiring additional current edits.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active RegulatedAuthorization source already provides the missing scope/context: a full Scope and Usage section covering regulated products, treatments, facilities, activities, and out-of-scope security/consent/contract/prescribing authorizations; the StructureDefinition description defines regulatory approval, clearance, or licensing; and the medication-definition module explains RegulatedAuthorization's relationship to neighboring medication-definition resources.
